posts.title: Meet Me at Midnight by Brianna Bourne - OPTIONAL
posts.description: Meet Me at Midnight by Brianna Bourne , 344 pages. Delacorte Press (Random House), 2026. $20 Language: R (6 swears, 10 f'); Mature Content: PG-13 (kissing, some drinking); Violence: G BUYING ADVISORY: MS, HS - OPTIONAL APPEALS TO: SEVERAL Every night at the stroke of midnight, 17yo Aria meets the boy of her dreams, Strat, in a different exotic location. But when she notices the logo on his school uniform, she decides to search for him in real life. As Aria begins to uncover the truth, she experiences memories of events she doesn't remember living through. Her conflicting memories of Strat leave her questioning what really happened between them and which memories she can trust. Meanwhile, Aria's twin sister, Cady, lies in a coma with little hope of recovery. As Aria struggles to piece together her past, she faces an impossible decision: hold on to the life she knows, with all its painful memories, or have everything erased and begin again. posts.title: Professor Thomas Cat's Guide to Understanding the Human Brain: The Dyslexia Files by Rachael Allen, PhD and Miguel Diaz Rivas
posts.description: Professor Thomas Cat's Guide to Understanding the Human Brain: The Dyslexia Files by Rachael Allen, PhD and Miguel Diaz Rivas . 144 pages. NON FICTION, GRAPHIC NOVEL. Magination Press, 2026. $19 Content: G BUYING ADVISORY: EL, MS - ESSENTIAL APPEALS TO: SOME In this nonfiction graphic novel, Professor Thomas Cat helps Ava understand how dyslexia makes her brain different from neurotypical brains. The book is packed with easy to understand information about how the brain works and why some brains process information differently. It explores both the challenges and advantages of dyslexia in a positive and encouraging way. Children will find helpful ideas and practical tips for coping with and embracing their diagnosis. I especially enjoyed the section at the end highlighting famous people with dyslexia and how they have used their unique strengths to accomplish great things. This is an uplifting and empowering book for children with dyslexia. Reviewer: A. Snow, Librarian

posts.title: Little Bones by Sandy Bigna - ADVISABLE
posts.description: Little Bones by Sandy Bigna , 239 pages. Simon & Schuster Books for Young Readers, 2026. $18 Content: G (no concerns) BUYING ADVISORY: EL - ADVISABLE APPEALS TO: SOME 11yo Bones got her nickname because of her passion for animal bones. She enjoys collecting and drawing animal skeletons. When her little brother passes away from an unfortunate accident, Bones' world is turned upside down. She loses her best friend and her mother leaves Bones with her grandma. Bones finds a skeleton of a small bird and wishes that it could be alive again. Surprisingly, her wish works but the bird is only a skeleton and wishes to return to his natural state. Can Bones and her new friend Tenny find a way to undo her wish? Little Bones was a very different and intriguing novel in verse. As Bones works through her grief, the reader follows her on a journey as she tries to let go of her skeleton bird and her depression of losing her brother. Drawings of skeletons are scattered throughout. Would be a great book
